entities.name: PMID:25448612
observations: ALSPAC birth-cohort study examined premorbid maternal and childhood psychological factors as predictors of chronic disabling fatigue at age 13 years.
Among 5,657 children, 110 (1.9%) met the chronic disabling fatigue definition: fatigue lasting at least 3 months, disabling school attendance or activities, and without another identified cause.
Maternal anxiety was associated with fatigue (adjusted OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.09–1.31 per episode); maternal depression was also associated (adjusted OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.11–1.39 per episode).

Child psychological problems were associated before maternal adjustment (adjusted OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.00–1.41 per problem), but attenuated after adjusting for maternal anxiety/depression (adjusted OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.93–1.33).
Upsetting life events showed a similar attenuation after maternal adjustment (adjusted OR 1.22, 95% CI 0.99–1.58 before; 1.19, 95% CI 0.94–1.52 after adjustment).
The observational longitudinal design supports prediction/association, not proof of causation.
